Moving to Portugal

Paperwork before you leave, transporting your belongings and the first formalities on arrival.

5 min read · Updated 14 October 2026

Need tailored advice?

France & Europe

Before you leave

  • Give notice, cancel or transfer your contracts, and report your change of address.
  • Check with your health insurance fund how you are covered abroad.
  • If you wish, register with the French consular register abroad: optional but useful for consular formalities.

Transporting your belongings

Within the European Union, personal belongings move without customs formalities. A detailed inventory is still essential: it is the reference at loading and delivery. Depending on volume, transport is by dedicated truck or by shared load, with other moves on the same route.

The historic centres of Lisbon and Porto have narrow, steep streets: access is assessed in advance, and the solution is set out in the quote.

On arrival

  • NIF: the Portuguese tax number, requested from the tax office (Finanças). It is needed for most formalities: lease, bank, contracts.
  • Registration certificate: after 3 months, EU citizens register with the town hall (Câmara Municipal) where they live. The certificate is valid for 5 years.

Cody’s tip

Our team speaks Portuguese: a real help when talking to neighbours or the caretaker on delivery day.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need to declare my furniture at customs?

No, between France and Portugal, both EU countries, personal belongings move without customs formalities.

What is a shared load?

Your furniture travels in a truck carrying several moves on the same route. It is often more economical for a moderate volume, with more flexible dates.

Official sources and references

  • UFE : s’installer au Portugal
  • Service-Public : je déménage en France

Information given as a guide, checked at the update date. Rules can change: check the source for your situation.
